response.message:
I've drawn the assistant on IBM Cloud: synthetic users sign in with App ID, a Code Engine app keeps each user's conversation in Cloudant, trims the context and calls a watsonx.ai model, and escalations go through Event Notifications to a support person. The first local test would use a scripted fake model to check sign-in handling, keeping each user's history separate, the context limit and the escalation path. That only tests our code, not real watsonx.ai quality, model access or IBM permissions, and nothing has been deployed or approved for a region or account.

Which country should the conversation data stay in, so we can pick the right IBM region?

proposal.body: End-to-end sketch: synthetic user → App ID sign-in → Code Engine assistant app → Cloudant per-user state, context bounding, watsonx.ai model, escalation through Event Notifications to a human queue, with logs in IBM Cloud Logs. No external actions. Assumptions: region to be selected; model choice, plan, quotas and IBM account access are unverified; there is no native generator for this workload yet, so engineering is required.

data.label: Synthetic user
data.description: Synthetic test person who chats through a browser. External caller, not provisioned.

data.label: Sign-in
data.description: Authenticates synthetic users (OIDC) and issues tokens. The app validates them before any chat turn. Anonymous access is denied.

data.label: Assistant app
data.description: Chat web app and API. It validates the App ID token, loads and saves per-user state, applies the context bound, calls the model, returns the answer and triggers escalation. It takes no external actions.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Per-user conversation documents, partitioned by user ID. A user can only read their own partition through the app.

data.label: Context bounder
data.description: Requested conceptual step owned by the assistant app. It caps history turns and tokens and screens input before the model call. Not a separate deployment.
data.service: Logic in the IBM Cloud Code Engine app

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Foundation model inference. The model, plan, region availability and quotas still need to be chosen and verified. Local tests use a scripted mock instead.

data.label: Escalation
data.description: Sends a handoff notice with a conversation reference when the user asks for a person or the app abstains.

data.label: Human support
data.description: Person or queue that receives escalations. External to the provisioning scope.

data.label: Logs & audit
data.description: Application logs, latency, errors and escalation audit, with no raw chat content by default.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If one user's history is shown to another user, that is a privacy breach. Unauthenticated access would bypass audit.
requirementDrafts.basis: "Build an authenticated conversational assistant" with "per-user conversation state"
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: only signed-in users can chat, and each user can read only their own conversation history.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Unbounded context raises cost and latency and can exceed the model's limits.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: each model call includes only a bounded amount of that user's recent history. The limit is still to be agreed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without escalation, users get stuck with wrong or empty answers.
requirementDrafts.basis: "an escalation path. No external actions in this first test."
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the user can request a person, and the app escalates when it cannot answer. Escalations are recorded, and no external actions are taken.

Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. response.message:
The emulation found no failures, and the IBM design itself is sound: every flow is connected and every component has a concrete service. It was blocked because the generator has no IBM templates for App ID, Code Engine, Cloudant, watsonx.ai or Event Notifications, and it has no reference plan for the synthetic user or the human support queue. That needs product work (new typed IBM implementations, tested with this same revision-2 project as the reproducer), not a diagram change, so I'm leaving the board as it is rather than cutting scope or switching to a storage-only contract.

While that engineering work is pending, we can still settle decisions that are ours to make: which country should the synthetic conversation data stay in, so we can later propose a matching IBM region?
